issues.description: The Bitmap24 class header in the template declares its constructors and member functions in a private section (making construction and public use of the class impossible), while the solution's header exposes these members as public. This conflicts with usage in main.cpp (instantiating Bitmap24 and calling resize_buffer/set), so students following the template will get access/visibility errors and be blocked from compiling or running the example program.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructors and public API of Bitmap24 public in the template header (e.g. add a public: label before width/height/data and the constructor/destructor/method declarations) so it matches the solution header and the usage sites in main.cpp. This will allow students to instantiate and use Bitmap24 as intended.
